change: SQLite JDBC — Distinguish SQL NULL from a zero-length BLOB
deployment: Both pinned Java trees with separately rebuilt Linux x86-64 JNI libraries over the setup's SQLite 3.9.1 amalgamation.
assumptions: Fresh in-memory database on Linux x86-64. The loaded sqlite native library must hash to the resource in the selected original JAR. SQL order is explicit.

questions.observer: Read the bytes and immediately call wasNull on each row of the same result set in ascending and reverse order.
questions.basis: Zero length is present, SQL NULL is absent, and five zero bytes keep their length and contents. Row order tests resetting wasNull.

questions.observer: Cross SQL NULL, a two-byte literal and a five-byte BLOB.
questions.basis: Both endpoints must preserve nullness and every nonempty byte.
